# Independent root audit: transport selection and centroid Jensen

The following are audited intermediate results, not a proof of OC.

## Trimmed target selection

`candidate 5cea8474957220e7` passes. The central marginal
sum is exactly twice the original central measure. Removing the
central-central block leaves strict-cross mass 1-2w, and the two leftover
marginals have exactly the masses needed by the opposite central parts.
Thus the stated family identity is exact, including the converse.

The partial coupling set is weakly compact. Closed-set payoffs and moving
closed cap payoffs are upper semicontinuous; their infimum is upper
semicontinuous. Hence the joint maximum exists. Finite cap duals use the
already proved finite-intersection and downward-payoff separation, not an
unjustified minimax interchange over all directions.

In each selection inequality the old pair projection is bounded by the
displayed unused-mass product times pi, and new marginal additions are
bounded by the displayed total-mass products times unused measures. The
chosen scaling simultaneously enforces removal and both marginal budgets.
All inequalities therefore hold for bounded Borel costs, including the
closed cap step functions. The center-repair extension retains the
forbidden central-central block because the residual central marginal
sum is at most the discarded pair mass.

For exact finite step costs, the essential minimum has positive selected
mass. Simultaneous unused replacement bounds the open cost on the entire
product of unused supports by lower semicontinuity. Those supports have
Lebesgue volumes at least their respective unused masses. Their midpoint
sum is in B. Ordinary Brunn-Minkowski, followed by discarding only finitely
many Lebesgue-null hyperplanes, proves the stated low-cost volume bound.
This last discard does not discard any target atom or change a closed
halfspace depth assertion.

## Shape obstructions

`candidate 39a2ef7b63aae46b` passes in its stated scopes. The
two-fiber example really fixes the median target to the first uniform
fiber. The one-dimensional mixture argument includes double-counted
boundary atoms. In the three-triangle example, the reflection overlap
formula is exact on [1/4,1/3], its density fits the marginal budgets, and
the midpoint atom has mass 1/2. Every triangle cap orientation is bounded
by the displayed vertex-cap and complementary-cap arguments. Thus the
trimmed optimum is exactly (4t^2+1/2)/(3/2), whose every positive power has
positive second derivative. No equality with the unrestricted optimum is
assumed.

## Conditional centroid Jensen

The main theorem of `candidate 82d7337f4dd32126` passes.
The cap-root function is concave on the nonempty convex cap domain and
upper semicontinuous, sufficient for its Jensen step. The conditional tail
variable is uniform on [0,1] for a positive full-dimensional convex fiber
and a nonzero continuous normal. The barycenter belongs to C and becomes
an actual point of S only under the stated integer-base assumption.
Purely integer normals are handled by ordinary fiber-root Jensen and
retain boundary mass. The effective count follows from Holder exactly.

the contributor found an algebra error in the original proof of the three-fiber
b/2 estimate. It has been repaired: weighted AM-GM gives the required
lower bound r^(-2/(r+2)), and calculus proves this exceeds 1/2 for r>=1.
The repaired case split is valid in every continuous dimension. It is
superseded for three consecutive fibers by the separate bounded-density
midpoint argument, once that argument's independent audit is complete.

The exact counterexample in `candidate 23e4866836fa0dcd`
was checked and its Fraction verifier run successfully. It disproves only
the stronger exploratory 1/3 guarantee at that centroid, not OC or a
maximum-depth assertion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
